evals.name: grain-or-not
evals.prompt: Without calling tools, decide whether a shopping cart should be a grain and what to consider.
evals.expected_output: Use a grain when there is a single-writer identity with state and behavior; check state placement, concurrency and lifetime.
assertions: Considers the entity identity as the grain key and single-threaded access as the benefit.
Considers where state lives and whether a database is better for it.
Names an alternative or tradeoff rather than asserting a grain unconditionally.

evals.name: cratis-edits
evals.prompt: Without calling tools, review a grain interface annotated with [Alias] that uses RegisterTimer for a periodic task.
evals.expected_output: Do not put [Alias] on grain interfaces or methods; no ConfigureAwait(false) in grain code; use RegisterGrainTimer for grain timers.
assertions: Does not endorse [Alias] on grain interfaces.
Does not endorse ConfigureAwait(false) in grain code, citing the Cratis Orleans rule.
Mentions a reminder or Durable Job if the schedule must survive deactivation.

evals.name: time-primitives
evals.prompt: Without calling tools, explain how timers, reminders and Durable Jobs differ.
evals.expected_output: Timers are in-memory and die with the activation; reminders persist; Durable Jobs schedule durable one-shot work.
assertions: States grain timers do not survive deactivation.
Maps scheduled one-time work to Durable Jobs.

evals.name: recoverable-jobs-ownership
evals.prompt: Without calling tools, a user wants a long import that resumes after a silo restart and suggests Orleans DurableJobs or Journaling. Who owns this and what do you say?
evals.expected_output: Defer recoverable job work to cratis-orleans-jobs; DurableJobs/Journaling are experimental and not interchangeable with Cratis.Orleans jobs.
assertions: Names cratis-orleans-jobs as the owner of recoverable job work.
States DurableJobs and Journaling are experimental.
States they are not interchangeable with Cratis.Orleans jobs.

evals.name: timer-and-placement-details
evals.prompt: Without calling tools, review a periodic batching timer and a claim that the default placement is random.
evals.expected_output: Callback is Func<CancellationToken, Task>; KeepAlive timers qualify activation liveness; resource-optimized is the default from Orleans 9.2, random before.
assertions: Uses the grain timer extension with a Func<CancellationToken, Task> callback.
Qualifies that KeepAlive timers affect activation liveness.
States resource-optimized placement is the default since Orleans 9.2 and random before.
